newsitem.title: SPAIN: LME seeks views on electronic warrant details -CEO.
newsitem.headline: LME seeks views on electronic warrant details -CEO.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) is seeking membership views on an automated system of recording warrant details, with a review likely to last four months, LME Chief Executive David King said.

"We are sending out a paper on the merits of introducing an electronic warrant deposit system. By September, the LME Board will be in a position to judge whether we go ahead," King said at Metal Bulletin's 10th International Copper Conference on Wednesday.

A metal warrant is a document akin to a stock bearer bond, which denotes the make of the particular material. These are currently physically switched between counter-parties, but under an automated system details and holdings would be recorded electronically.
Although the LME has not yet decided on whether to publicise warrant ownership -- which is curently confidential -- an electronic system would make this easier, King said.

The LME is considering these issues in the light of the review by the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) last December. The exchange called for the review in the wake of the Sumitomo Corp copper trading scandal, and is currently instituting a package of reforms.
Some measures have been introduced since January, while others are still pending.
King said the expansion of the LME board, which has been implemented, was evolutionary rather than revolutionary.
The LME had yet to decide how to address market intervention, currently carried out by the Board.
"We have to seek a mechanism for market intervention, but we have yet to work out a method to avoid conflict of interests," he said.
When the SIB reforms were finally implemented, the LME would be in a better position to address the question of market abuse, he added.
